title: triggers on bank: who fires when, an audit table, 20,000 rows row by row or all at once, and skipping no-op updates

steps.sql: BEGIN
steps.note: a transaction, so the firing-order triggers disappear afterwards.
four triggers on accounts that all write to one log: before and after, statement and row.

steps.sql: UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 1 WHERE id IN (1, 2, 3)
steps.note: one UPDATE of three rows.

steps.sql: SELECT seq, trigger_when, level, account FROM fired ORDER BY seq
steps.note: the order they fired in.

steps.sql: ROLLBACK
steps.note: undo.
an audit table, and a row trigger that writes to it on every insert, update and delete.

steps.sql: SELECT id, account_id, op, old_balance, new_balance FROM accounts_audit ORDER BY id
steps.note: the audit table starts empty.

steps.sql:
UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + CASE id WHEN 1 THEN -50.00 ELSE 50.00 END
WHERE id IN (1, 2)
steps.note: alice pays bob 50.00, in one statement that updates two rows. the trigger fires once per row.

steps.sql: SELECT id, account_id, op, old_balance, new_balance FROM accounts_audit ORDER BY id
steps.note: two audit rows, old and new balance side by side.

steps.sql: DELETE FROM accounts WHERE id = 3
steps.note: carol closes her account.

steps.sql: SELECT id, account_id, op, old_balance, new_balance FROM accounts_audit ORDER BY id
steps.note: a DELETE has only an old row.

steps.sql:
INSERT INTO accounts (id, owner, opening_balance, balance, opened_at)
VALUES (1001, 'erin', 25.00, 25.00, '2026-05-01 10:00+00')
steps.note: erin opens one.

steps.sql: SELECT id, account_id, op, old_balance, new_balance FROM accounts_audit ORDER BY id
steps.note: an INSERT has only a new row.

steps.sql: DROP TRIGGER audit ON accounts
steps.note: the audit trigger goes, so the next scenes don't write to it.

steps.sql: BEGIN
steps.note: a transaction for the row-trigger run.
a row-level trigger on transfers that copies every changed row into an audit table, and counts its own calls.

steps.sql: UPDATE transfers SET amount = amount + 1
steps.note: every transfer, 20,000 rows.

steps.sql: SELECT nextval('trigger_calls') - 1 AS calls, (SELECT count(*) FROM transfers_audit) AS audit_rows
steps.note: the trigger function ran 20,000 times, and ran 20,000 single-row INSERTs.

steps.sql: ROLLBACK
steps.note: undo.

steps.sql: BEGIN
steps.note: a transaction for the statement-trigger run.
the same audit as a statement-level trigger: REFERENCING gives it every old and new row of the statement as two tables.

steps.sql: UPDATE transfers SET amount = amount + 1
steps.note: every transfer, 20,000 rows.

steps.sql: SELECT nextval('trigger_calls') - 1 AS calls, (SELECT count(*) FROM transfers_audit) AS audit_rows
steps.note: one call, one INSERT ... SELECT, the same 20,000 audit rows.

steps.sql: ROLLBACK
steps.note: undo.

steps.sql: SELECT id, currency, ctid, xmin FROM accounts WHERE id IN (1, 2, 4) ORDER BY id
steps.note: three accounts: where each version lives (ctid) and which transaction wrote it (xmin).

steps.sql: UPDATE accounts SET currency = currency
steps.note: an UPDATE that changes nothing: currency = currency, on every account.

steps.sql: SELECT id, currency, ctid, xmin FROM accounts WHERE id IN (1, 2, 4) ORDER BY id
steps.note: every row has a new ctid and a new xmin anyway: a whole new version was written, 1,000 times.

steps.sql:
CREATE TRIGGER skip_noop BEFORE UPDATE ON accounts
FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION suppress_redundant_updates_trigger()
steps.note: a BEFORE UPDATE trigger running the built-in suppress_redundant_updates_trigger().

steps.sql: UPDATE accounts SET currency = currency
steps.note: the same no-op UPDATE. the trigger sees new = old, returns NULL, and the row is skipped. UPDATE 0.

steps.sql: SELECT id, currency, ctid, xmin FROM accounts WHERE id IN (1, 2, 4) ORDER BY id
steps.note: nothing written: same ctids, same xmins.

steps.sql: UPDATE accounts SET currency = 'USD' WHERE id = 4
steps.note: a real change still goes through.

steps.sql: SELECT id, currency, ctid, xmin FROM accounts WHERE id IN (1, 2, 4) ORDER BY id
steps.note: one new version, for dave.
